title: Impurity as a probe of Berry curvature and wavefunction winding in gapped two-band models
authors: Reda Nabil, Pascal Simon, Andrej Mesaros
abstract: We explore the possibility of using quasiparticle interference near impurities to extract non-local properties of bands. Focusing on the minimal two-band description of a system with multiple valleys, we show that the local density of states (LDOS) induced by non-magnetic impurities can effectively probe both the Berry curvature and the wavefunction winding, locally in each valley. We analyze gapped models based on Dirac, semi-Dirac, quadratic touching, and higher-order touching energy dispersions, in presence of a point-like potential scatterer. We find that for strong enough impurity potentials the LDOS along a contour around the impurity unambiguously shows the wavefunction winding number, in contrast to the case of gapless Dirac-like dispersions where the winding can be precluded by LDOS oscillations in the radial direction. We also establish a general connection between, on the one hand, the Berry curvature as a function of momentum locally in a valley, and on the other hand, the wavefunction winding number and the energy dispersion parameters, making hence the local Berry curvature directly observable from spectroscopic LDOS information.
summary: This work demonstrates that the local density of states (LDOS) around impurities in gapped two-band materials can serve as a spectroscopic probe for non-local topological properties like the Berry curvature and wavefunction winding number. By analyzing the impurity-induced bound states, the authors establish a general relationship allowing the direct measurement of the Berry curvature from spectroscopic measurements.
main_problem: The paper investigates using quasiparticle interference (QPI) near impurities to extract non-local topological properties, specifically the Berry curvature and wavefunction winding number, in gapped two-band electronic models.
main_result: It establishes a direct, local connection showing that the Berry curvature can be unambiguously extracted from the spectroscopic Local Density of States (LDOS) induced by impurities, particularly in gapped systems.
method: The analysis employs the T-matrix formalism applied to the Green's function of the system, linearizing the Bloch Hamiltonian at high-symmetry points (valleys) to derive a continuum model.
model_or_system: The study focuses on minimal two-band models derived from lattice structures like the honeycomb lattice (e.g., hBN, TMDs), encompassing various dispersion types (Dirac, semi-Dirac, quadratic) parameterized by gap, winding number, and dispersion exponent.
key_observables: Local Density of States (LDOS) induced by impurities, wavefunction winding number (W), and Berry curvature ($\Omega$).
important_parameters: Gap ($\Delta_Q$), winding number ($W_Q$), and the strength of the impurity potential ($V$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on low-energy continuum expansions around high-symmetry points and assumes the impurity potential is strong enough to reveal the topological winding number.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the comparison between analytical continuum predictions and tight-binding results, and show the dependence of the winding region on filtering parameters.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by deriving the low-energy continuum Hamiltonian from lattice structure factors, calculating the real-space Green's function, and finally using the T-matrix formalism to determine the impurity-induced LDOS and extract the topological invariants.
why_interesting: The direct link established between a measurable spectroscopic quantity (LDOS) and a fundamental topological invariant (Berry curvature) provides a powerful, experimentally testable theoretical tool for condensed matter physics.

FIG. 4. Winding region in real space according to analytical low-energy theory of the hBN model. For a given impurity potential V producing a bound state at energy ωb (vertical axis), a circle of radius r (horizontal axis) detects a wavefront dislocation (region ”Winding” in plot) if the LDOS terms satisfy δρB(r, ωb) > δρA(r, ωb) (see text). The ”Winding” region corresponds to strong impurity potential (see Fig. 2).

Figure 4 reveals the real space region in which the LDOS of an impurity with potential V exhibits a wave- front dislocation, in the case of the illustrative low-energy hBN model. For the given value of V we find the bound state energy ωb from Eq. (25) (see Fig. 2a), and then we find the winding region as the set of distances r for which δρB(r, ωb) > δρA(r, ωb). Above a critical impurity strength Vc, the condition δρB(r, ωb) > δρA(r, ωb) is satisfied for all distances r, such that the winding is, in principle, observable on any loop around the impurity.
